q: Our boiler burns only biomass. Do we still have Scope 1 emissions?
title: Biomass boilers and Scope 1
short: Yes, a little. The CO2 from burning biomass is reported separately as biogenic, outside the Scope 1 total, but methane and nitrous oxide from combustion stay in Scope 1. IPCC defaults for wood are 30 kg methane and 4 kg nitrous oxide per terajoule, roughly 2 tonnes of CO2e per terajoule.
audience: MSMEs running husk, wood, briquette or bagasse boilers

ol: Tonnes of biomass times its net calorific value gives terajoules.
Times 30 kg CH4 and 4 kg N2O per TJ.
Convert with global warming potentials, stating which IPCC report you used.

ul: Scope 1 CO2e from methane and nitrous oxide.
Any fossil fuel used for start-up, such as diesel or coal.

p: Buyers and verifiers ask where it came from. Keep supplier invoices and note whether it is residue, waste or plantation wood.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel invoices, gas bills and delivery documents into dated, fingerprinted records, so each tonne of CO2 traces back to the document behind it.
